pictures.scene: Aelbert Cuyp, The Maas at Dordrecht — the wide river lying still against its own shore in golden light, He set the earth on its foundations, never to be moved
pictures.name: pd_cuyp_grens

pictures.scene: Claude-Joseph Vernet, A Shipwreck in Stormy Seas — the sea coming over everything under a black sky, You covered it with the deep like a garment, the waters stood above the mountains
pictures.name: pd_vernet_diep

pictures.scene: Albert Bierstadt, A Storm in the Rocky Mountains — the storm cloud piled higher than the peaks and the water lying below, at Your rebuke the waters fled, at the sound of Your thunder they hurried away
pictures.name: pd_bierstadt_bergen

pictures.scene: Thomas Moran, The Chasm of the Colorado — the gorge cut down through the rock under a breaking storm, the mountains rose and the valleys sank, to the place You assigned for them
pictures.name: pd_moran_donder

pictures.scene: Allaert van Everdingen, Landscape with a Waterfall — the spring water coming down over the rocks out of the high ground, You set a boundary they cannot cross, that they may never again cover the earth
pictures.name: pd_everdingen_bron

pictures.scene: Paulus Potter, Cows near a Farm — the cattle standing at the water's edge in the heat of the day, He sends forth springs in the valleys, they flow between the mountains
pictures.name: pd_potter_drenken

pictures.scene: Melchior d'Hondecoeter, Water Birds — ducks and herons and every kind of bird gathered at the pool, they give drink to every beast of the field, the wild donkeys quench their thirst
pictures.name: pd_hondecoeter_vogels

pictures.scene: Asher Brown Durand, In the Woods — the green shade of the deep forest with the stream running under the fallen trunks, the birds of the air nest beside the springs, they sing among the branches
pictures.name: pd_durand_takken

pictures.scene: Charles-Émile Jacque, Sheep at Pasture — the flock spread out over good grass with the shepherd behind them, He waters the mountains from His chambers, the earth is satisfied by the fruit of His works
pictures.name: pd_jacque_gras

lines.text: He set the earth on its foundations,
You covered it with the deep like a garment;
the waters stood above the mountains.
At Your rebuke the waters fled;
at the sound of Your thunder they hurried away—
the mountains rose and the valleys sank
to the place You assigned for them—
You set a boundary they cannot cross,
that they may never again cover the earth.
He sends forth springs in the valleys;
They give drink to every beast of the field;
the wild donkeys quench their thirst.
The birds of the air nest beside the springs;
He waters the mountains from His chambers;
the earth is satisfied by the fruit of His works.
